title: Whole Asymmetric Footplate and Open Crura Stapes
description: One wholly newly authored greatly enlarged detached stapes-bone teaching schematic, about ten centimetres tall rather than life size. A full subtly curved asymmetric oval footplate retains a finite rim and thicker posterior area. Two complete tapering crura form a real central opening; the posterior crus bows more than the anterior and both retain finite inward-facing grooves. Their full lower ends are embedded in the footplate, and the upper shoulders join one complete slightly offset head and constricted neck with a shallow articular depression. Footplate, crural paths, grooves and head profile are independently drawn; no riding stirrup, leather, metal ring, former bone, organelle or old asset component is extracted or relabelled. One whole bone model, zero scenes, with two quiet opaque bone-like PBR roles. This is an artistic external-morphology diagram, not a scan, exact human specimen, universal anatomical shape, ear assembly or patient-specific model. Cartilage, annular ligament, muscle, vessels, marrow microstructure and neighbouring ossicles are omitted. The lowest footplate point is only an art datum, not a natural standing posture. No medical advice, diagnostic use, prosthesis fit, surgery, hearing mechanics, sound simulation, strength, rig or animation is claimed.
